claims.text: Tailored heat treatment can systematically vary and optimize local chemical order in FCC high-entropy alloys.
Optimizing local chemical order through heat treatment will simultaneously increase yield strength and ductility under high-strain-rate deformation.
The target initial material is an as-cast or homogenized single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy with inherent lattice distortion.
Dynamic high-strain-rate testing can be performed with a split-Hopkinson bar at ambient and moderately varied temperatures.
Heat treatment produces nanoclusters with specific forms of short-range chemical order.
Local-chemical-order nanoclusters modify dislocation slip pathways.
Local chemical order modulates dynamic recovery processes.
An optimal degree of local chemical order creates a favorable balance between lattice resistance and dislocation mobility.
The local-chemical-order-induced change in dislocation behavior enhances strain hardening.
Optimized local chemical order will produce higher yield strength than the untreated baseline during dynamic loading.
Optimized local chemical order will produce greater uniform elongation than the untreated baseline during dynamic loading.
Optimized local chemical order will increase activation of dynamic recovery mechanisms.
The proposed effect should hold from ambient to moderately cryogenic temperatures.
The proposed local-chemical-order benefit may not apply under quasi-static loading.
The effect may not transfer to alloys with substantially different compositions or grain sizes.
Grain size and compositional complexity may influence the magnitude of the mechanical-property response.

A lack of systematic improvement in both yield strength and ductility, or a lack of a correlated shift in dislocation mechanisms, across controlled local-chemical-order levels would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The comparator is repeatedly called untreated, but the baseline also describes it as having a conventional heat-treatment state. It is therefore unclear whether the control receives no heat treatment or a non-LCO-optimized heat treatment.
